sources.note: Vehes occurs only in cognate sets and sound-correspondence tables (pp. 133-134, 140, 154, 158, 399, 407; its data are Hooley 1971 wordlists, p. 407). No statement about Vehes stress. The only prosodic remark for the subgroup is a proto-language one (p. 157): 'Unstressed vowels were deleted or became a non-phonemic schwa (re-phonemicised in some daughter-languages) in Proto Hote/Buang, creating consonant clusters' — not a stress-placement rule for Vehes.

sources.note: Entry '37. VEHES' gives numerals 1-5 and 10 taken from Hooley's (1971) wordlists (timu, uy, yar, nyekuy, nema baru, nema yin). Nothing on phonology or stress (all 'stress' hits are the ordinary verb).

sources.note: The sole first-hand Vehes data (survey wordlist, c. 200 items) and the source behind every later citation of Vehes forms (Ross 1988, Smith 1988, ASJP). A lexicostatistical survey, so a stress statement is unlikely, but it is the only place a first-hand phonological remark on Vehes could exist.
